task_completion.description: Open the 'Edit Visualisation' or 'View Settings' dialog in sumo-gui.
task_completion.visual_evidence: A pop-up window titled 'View Settings' or 'Edit Visualisation' is visible over the main SUMO interface.

task_completion.description: Navigate to the 'Vehicles' tab within the visualization settings.
task_completion.visual_evidence: The 'Vehicles' tab is selected/active in the View Settings dialog.

task_completion.description: Change the vehicle coloring attribute to 'speed'.
task_completion.visual_evidence: A dropdown menu or selection box for vehicle 'Color' or 'Color by' shows 'speed' as the selected option.

task_completion.description: Start the simulation to populate the network with vehicles.
task_completion.visual_evidence: The simulation time/step counter is increasing, and vehicles are visible moving on the road network.

task_completion.description: Confirm vehicles are colored according to their speed (multi-colored fleet).
task_completion.visual_evidence: Vehicles in the viewport appear in different colors (e.g., a gradient from red to yellow/green) rather than a uniform default color.

task_completion.description: Execute the command to save the screenshot to the specific path.
task_completion.visual_evidence: A terminal window shows the execution of a screenshot command (like 'scrot') targeting '/home/ga/SUMO_Output/speed_coloring.png'.

integrity.description: The agent interacted with the sumo-gui menus rather than just using CLI tools to generate an image.
integrity.visual_evidence: Screenshots show the mouse cursor or highlighted menu items within the sumo-gui 'View Settings' dialog.

integrity.description: The agent is working with the Bologna Acosta network, not a default or empty network.
integrity.visual_evidence: The road layout in the GUI matches a complex real-world urban intersection (Bologna Acosta) rather than a simple grid or single road.

integrity.description: The agent did not simply rename an existing image to the target filename.
integrity.visual_evidence: The sequence of screenshots shows the GUI state changing (coloring settings) followed by the screenshot command being typed/executed.

privileged_info_for_vlm: The task requires using the 'Bologna Acosta' scenario, which is pre-loaded in sumo-gui. The agent must specifically change the vehicle coloring mode to 'speed' in the View Settings (Vehicles tab). The final output must be a screenshot saved to /home/ga/SUMO_Output/speed_coloring.png showing the simulation running with multi-colored vehicles representing different speeds.
